name: Hua Hin
tagline: Royal seaside town with night markets and national parks
summary: Hua Hin has been Thailand's royal seaside resort for a century. See the striking red-and-white railway station, wander the teak Maruekhathaiyawan Palace, eat at the Cicada and night markets, and day-trip to the cave temple of Phraya Nakhon in Sam Roi Yot National Park, where light pours onto a golden pavilion.
seasonNote: November to March is driest; the Gulf coast stays fairly dry in the western monsoon.
arrival: About 3 hours by road or train from Bangkok.
gettingAround: Songthaews and Grab in town; car for national parks.
cashTip: Carry baht for street food, tuk-tuks and boats; cards work in hotels and malls. Tipping is small and optional.
foodTip: Seafood on the piers, pla neung manao (lime-steamed fish) and night-market snacks.
buyTip: Crafts and art at Cicada Market.
